When Tool Names Are Not Identities: Measuring Provider Misbinding in MCP-Based AI Agents
description: Large language model (LLM) applications increasingly act as agents that select and invoke external tools. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) standardizes this interaction by allowing clients to compose tools advertised by multiple servers. authors: Zeynab Anbiaee, Sajjad Dadkhah, Ali A. Ghorbani

title: Experience Rot: Experienced Agents Fail Where Novices Succeed
description: Agents are increasingly built to learn from experience: they keep conversation histories, memory files, retrieved notes and skills, and reuse what worked before. We show that this experience turns against them when their tools change silently. We test a range of models with tools defined as in the Model Context Protocol (MCP). authors: Zhen Xu, Hang Yin, Zitao Zhang

title: Type-Confusion Security
description: Type systems are a lightweight way to obtain formal assurance that code upholds security properties. However, decentralized systems, such as smart contracts and Model Context Protocol ecosystems, have limited ability to constrain the behavior of untrusted code.
